svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Peristalsis moves food along the gut, here the oesophagus."], [1, "Circular muscle contracts just behind the bolus: the gut narrows and squeezes the food forward."], [4, "In front of the bolus, circular muscle relaxes and longitudinal muscle contracts: the gut widens."], [7, "The wave of contraction travels along the gut, carrying the bolus with it."], [11, "It is involuntary smooth muscle, and works even upside down."]]
svg.title: Peristalsis
svg.desc: A section of oesophagus with a bolus pushed along by a wave of circular muscle contraction behind it and longitudinal muscle contraction in front, plus a cross-section of the gut wall.
svg.text: Section along the oesophagus (cut lengthways); food moves left to right, towards the stomach.

g.data-info: Contracts in front of the bolus, shortening and widening that section so the food can move in.
Contracts behind the bolus, squeezing the lumen narrow and pushing the food forward; relaxes in front of it.
Mucus from goblet cells lubricates the bolus.
A soft ball of chewed food mixed with saliva.
Smooth muscle; involuntary, coordinated by the nerves in the gut wall. In the oesophagus a bolus reaches the stomach in about 8–10 s; peristalsis works even upside down.
From the lumen outward: mucosa, submucosa, circular muscle, longitudinal muscle.

g.text: • Behind the bolus: circular muscle contracts, longitudinal relaxes → gut narrows.
• In front of the bolus: circular muscle relaxes, longitudinal contracts → gut widens.
• The two layers are antagonistic; the wave is involuntary (enteric nerves).
• Peristalsis also moves food through the stomach and intestines, and urine down the ureters.
